scientific_question: Can explicit base-model relational representation supervision produce held-out counterfactual identity selection and improve native output, when the experiment is actually valid (disjoint names/families, seed-specific schedules, complete evaluator)?
sole_intervention: parameter-free normalized query-to-candidate pointer loss added to the frozen T2 candidate-margin treatment; binding/localizer remains frozen

parent.lineage: Phase1G U6000 best; no T2 descendant

objective.native: T2 length-normalized hardest-distractor pairwise margin hinge, M=1.0; no prompt/continuation CE, no EOS supervision, no KL, no localization term
objective.pointer: q=final_norm at BOS-prefixed index len(prompt_token_ids); k+/k- = mean final_norm over first defining name-token span excluding punctuation; L_ptr=-log softmax cosine; gradients to q and both anchors; no trainable pointer head

seeds.schedule_rule: seed-specific deterministic permutation of the identical frozen train corpus; language rehearsal windows shared

corpus.acq16: 4 train families, assignment x query at fact_order=0 (16 rows), included in training

gates.language: DEV CE <= min(1.30, own U0 + 0.25); terminal train-dev gap <= 0.5
gates.binding: all non-base_model parameters byte-identical to parent at every eval; NOT_APPLICABLE_UNTRAINED behaviorally
gates.shortcut: if representation gates would pass but a nuisance probe accuracy is within 0.02 of pointer retrieval, classify T3_SHORTCUT_FAILURE

stopping.u100: descriptive; stop only nonfinite, binding-identity break, or DEV CE > 1.50
stopping.terminal: classify at U500 from frozen gates; no post-result rescue
stopping.test_policy: TEST scored once only after terminal DEV commit and only if DEV representation AND native gates pass
